terra.problem: The text says all the people came to Jesus, but it says nothing about seats or whether any were empty.
The cookie and clipboard comparison does not clearly picture a question meant to trap someone.
The passage gives the scribes and Pharisees' reason for asking, but does not say nobody there was taking notes to learn.
The passage does not say the whole mood changed.
Jesus did not ask who was without sin. He directed the one without sin to cast the first stone.
The passage says the scribes and Pharisees were testing Jesus. It does not say Jesus was testing them.
The passage does not say there was no shouting or speech, or that the crowd was quiet.
The passage does not describe the accusation as loud or the people leaving as quiet.
The passage does not say whether anyone stopped to pray.
The text says they left beginning with the older ones, not that the oldest person left first.
The scribes and Pharisees brought the woman; the text does not say a crowd dragged her in. It also does not describe Jesus' tone as gentle.
The passage does not say the accusers came to condemn her. Her answer says no one condemned her, not that they were gone.
The text says the scribes and Pharisees brought her, not a whole crowd. Jesus was still there with her, so it is misleading to say nobody was left to condemn her.
Jesus' statement that He does not condemn her and His direction to sin no more are two sentences, not one.
The statement that sacrifices come up often in the Law is a Bible fact from outside this passage and needs a reference.
